statement: For an iid uniform {-1,+1} 2x2 matrix M, P(s_min(M)<=epsilon/sqrt(2)) is 1/2 for 0<=epsilon<2 and 1 for epsilon>=2.
source: Independent derivation: columns are proportional with probability 1/2; otherwise their inner product is zero and M^T M=2I.
proof_or_counterexample: Two columns lie in the same one-dimensional sign class in 8 of 16 matrices, giving s_min=0. In the other 8 they are orthogonal with squared norm 2, giving s_min=sqrt(2). Thus the scaled variable sqrt(2)*s_min has atoms 0 and 2, both of mass 1/2.
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap in the elementary derivation; independent review and computational cross-check pending. This is a boundary special case, not a novelty claim or a solution of C0029.

statement: Uniform comparison H(t)<=F_n(t)<=(1+delta_n)H(t)+exp(-n), with H(t)=1-exp(-t-t*t/2) and delta_n=(log(n+e))^(-1/16), does not imply F_n(t)<=t+C*exp(-c*n) uniformly in t>=0 for any fixed C,c>0.
assumptions: abstract scalar CDFs, not iid matrix laws
source: Independent derivation saved before paired proof in ATTEMPT.md; explicit CDF construction.
proof_or_counterexample: F_n(t)=exp(-n)+(1-exp(-n))*H((1+delta_n)*t). At t=sqrt(delta_n)/2 excess >=delta_n**1.5/6. Concavity of H establishes the uniform relative comparison.
remaining_gap: Referee check pending. Does not refute exact finite-n Gaussian comparison or the Rademacher conjecture.

statement: For every even n>=2 there is a full-row-rank (n-1) by n sign matrix A with kernel spanned by the perfectly flat unit vector (1,...,1)/sqrt(n), for which an independent iid Rademacher row X has P(dist(X,rowspan(A))=0)=binom(n,n/2)/2^n>=1/(n+1).
assumptions: fixed A built from independent balanced sign rows
proof_or_counterexample: Balanced rows span the zero-sum hyperplane: differences include 2(e_i-e_j). Select a basis. The projection vanishes exactly when X is balanced. See ATTEMPT.md B03.
remaining_gap: Independent w572 review pending. Conditional obstruction only; no averaged or parent-problem refutation.

statement: H(t)=1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is not the exact finite-n least-singular-value CDF of real iid standard Gaussian matrices. At n=1 the CDF is erf(t/sqrt(2)), with derivative sqrt(2/pi) at zero instead of one.
proof_or_counterexample: The single singular value of [Z] is |Z|. Integrate the standard Gaussian density. The finite-n versus limit distinction is explicitly stated in Rudelson-Vershynin ICM 2010 Theorem 3.1 and (3.2), p.9.
